claim: measured_outcomes, 'Vendor benchmarks' entry: 'Qwen3-VL-2B reaches ~180 tok/s generation on NVIDIA's TensorRT Edge-LLM reference setup' (cited to https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-vl-3b).
problem: The cited source does not contain this number - I re-opened the Liquid AI blog and it reports only LFM2.5-VL-3B figures plus an H100 vLLM comparison; there is no Qwen3-VL-2B TensorRT Edge-LLM throughput anywhere on the page. Checking NVIDIA's actual TensorRT Edge-LLM benchmark page, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct decodes at about 151 tok/s on Jetson AGX Thor (BS=1, INT4 AWQ/FP16), ~150 on DGX Spark, ~98.9 on AGX Orin and ~58.5 on Orin NX; the ~180.8 tok/s figure appears only in the older v0.4.0 NVFP4 results. So the number is both unsourced at the citation given and stale relative to the current benchmark. This is a number attached to a source that does not support it.
fix: Either delete the Qwen3-VL-2B clause, or cite https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-Edge-LLM/user_guide/performance/performance-benchmarks.html and state the device-specific current figure (e.g. 'Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct decodes at ~151 tok/s on Jetson AGX Thor, batch size 1, INT4 AWQ') with the caveat that ~180 tok/s comes from older v0.4.0 NVFP4 results. Split the LFM2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL numbers into separate entries so each carries the URL that actually states it.

claim: fit_score rationale: legal_risk_low 9/15 is described as 'deliberately kept in the lower half'.
problem: Arithmetic is fine (15+13+9+13+9+9 = 68 of 100, and the /20 and /15 ceilings quoted in the rationale match the sub-scores), but 9/15 is 60%, i.e. above the midpoint of its own scale, so the 'lower half' description contradicts the score. Minor: the score itself is defensible against the legal section (criminal exposure under N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9, an unverified negative finding on notice, a rescinded NLRB GC memo).
fix: Reword to 'kept below the level the other sub-scores suggest' and/or drop legal_risk_low to 7 (total 66), rather than claiming it sits in the lower half.

claim: measured_outcomes, 'Detector latencies' entry: 'Coral ~10 ms with the default model (Frigate caps a Coral at 1000/inference-ms fps)'.
problem: The Frigate hardware page states the 1000/inference-ms cap, but the '~10 ms' is the page's own worked example ('With an inference speed of 10, your Coral will top out at 100 frames per second'), not a benchmarked Coral latency - the table carries no Coral ms column. Presented as a measured latency it overstates the source.
fix: Say 'Frigate's docs use an inference speed of 10 ms for a Coral as their worked example (cap = 1000/inference-ms fps)' or drop the figure and keep the cap rule.
